1.note: The command forms such as **shout** are plural in this psalm because the psalmist is calling all people to praise God, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. See how “shout” is translated in Psalms 47:1. Alternate translation: [Raise a shout to Yahweh]

Here, **all the earth** represents all the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all people on earth]

2.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **gladness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [gladly]

Here, **to his face** represents being in the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [into his presence]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rejoicing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [singing joyful songs]

3.note: The word translated as **Know** is a command. If, in your language, someone would not command someone else to know something, then use a form in your language that communicates an exhortation to fully realize something. Alternate translation: [Let us fully realize] or [You must believe that it is true]

The pronouns **Yahweh** and **he** both refer to God. The psalmist is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though it could be omitted, in order to emphasize that it is Yahweh specifically who is God. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the emphasis here. Alternate translation: [it is Yahweh who is God]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he made us** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Yahweh is the one who made us and no one else. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [he is the one who made us]

Many ancient manuscripts read **and not we**. The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “and we are his.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT. Alternate translation: [and we are his]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and it was not we who made ourselves]

The psalmist is speaking here as if the people were actually **sheep** that belong to God. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he provides for us as though we were sheep in his pasture]

4.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **thanksgiving**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as you thank him]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **praise**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as you praise him]
Here, **his name** represents who he is. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [him]

5.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [It is right to do this since]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **eternity**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [he is eternally faithful to his covenant]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **eternity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is everlasting]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truthfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he is trustworthy] or [he is truthful]

The psalmist is using **generation and generation** as a common expression of his culture to mean “for all time” or “forever.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and his truthfulness endures for all time]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and his truthfulness lasts until generation and generation]
